name: Johnnie Cake
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Sift one quart of Indian meal into a pan
make a hole in the middle and pour in a pint of warm water, adding one teaspoonful of salt
with a spoon mix the meal and water gradually into a soft dough
stir it very briskly for a quarter of an hour or more, till it becomes light and spongy
spread the dough smoothly and evenly on a straight, flat board (a piece of the head of a flour-barrel will serve for this purpose)
place the board nearly upright before an open fire and put an iron against the back to support it
when done, cut it in squares
send it hot to table, split and buttered

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Sift one quart of Indian meal into a pan
2. make a hole in the middle and pour in a pint of warm water, adding one teaspoonful of salt
3. with a spoon mix the meal and water gradually into a soft dough
4. stir it very briskly for a quarter of an hour or more, till it becomes light and spongy
5. spread the dough smoothly and evenly on a straight, flat board (a piece of the head of a flour-barrel will serve for this purpose)
6. place the board nearly upright before an open fire and put an iron against the back to support it
7. bake it well
8. when done, cut it in squares
9. send it hot to table, split and buttered
